items.prompt:
# Sort the reconciliation screen alphabetically by "Your mod"

Director's own request, live-testing feedback: `msRenderReconcile()` in `app.js` currently renders
`msReport.review` in whatever order `buildMatchReport` produced it (effectively user-file key
insertion order). The director wants it sorted alphabetically by `row.userName` ("Your mod") instead
-- two similarly-named mods (e.g. a "- 2k" and "- 4k" variant of the same base name, or any other
near-duplicate naming) currently land in unrelated positions on the screen, making it hard to spot
that they're related at a glance. Sorting alphabetically puts near-duplicate names next to each
other, which is exactly the situation this reconciliation screen most needs extra scrutiny for (see
the just-fixed patchable-false leak this same session, which was made harder to notice for exactly
this reason).

Note this repo's existing convention for this exact kind of thing: `buildReport`'s exact-match
bucket already sorts this way at render time --
`msReport.exact.slice().sort(function (a, b) { return a.userName.localeCompare(b.userName); })`
(app.js, around the `bucketExactList` render). Apply the same pattern to `msRenderReconcile`'s own
render loop: sort a COPY of `msReport.review` by `row.userName` (localeCompare, matching the
existing convention -- don't introduce ordinal comparison here, that's a different, deliberate
convention used elsewhere for a different reason, see PGPatcher's own real sort order) before
iterating to build rows. Do NOT mutate `msReport.review` itself in place -- other code (candidate
counts, the Continue-button pending-count check, `removeCandidateEverywhere`) may depend on it
keeping its original array identity/order; sort a `.slice()` the same way the exact-bucket render
already does.

## Verify

- Load a real report with several review-tier rows whose `userName`s are NOT already alphabetical
  in the current UI, confirm they render in alphabetical order after the change.
- Confirm confirming/declining/undoing a row still works correctly after the sort (i.e. the sort is
  purely a render-order change, not a change to how rows are identified/matched/confirmed).
- Confirm nothing else that reads `msReport.review`'s order (the Continue button's pending-count
  nudge, `initializeSortState`) is affected -- it shouldn't be, since only the render loop's local
  iteration order changes, not the underlying array.

Write the usual handoff when done.

# Handoff — Sort the reconciliation screen alphabetically by "Your mod"
